title: There are questions people whisper in private but are too afraid to ask out loud in church… and this is one of them.
paragraphs: There are questions people whisper in private but are too afraid to ask out loud in church… and this is one of them.
Does masturbation always involve lust… or have we misunderstood something deeper about the human heart?

Because if we’re honest… this isn’t just about an action.
It’s about what’s happening inside us when no one is watching.
And that’s where everything changes.
The kind of change that exposes… then heals.
The kind that feels uncomfortable before it feels freeing.
The kind Jesus always brings.

“WHEN NO ONE IS WATCHING: THE QUESTION WE’RE AFRAID TO ASK”
The hidden tension between desire, purity, and the God who sees everything.
There’s a moment in the Gospel where Jesus completely shifts how sin is understood. Not outward. Not behavioral. But inward… surgical… unavoidable.
In Matthew 5:28, He says:
“But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart.”
The Greek doesn’t soften it. It sharpens it.

“πᾶς ὁ βλέπων γυναῖκα πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτὴν…”
(Pas ho blepōn gunaika pros to epithymēsai autēn…)
That phrase “πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι” (pros to epithymēsai) means more than noticing beauty. It means intentional desire… a willful internal pursuit… a deliberate stirring of craving.
It’s not the presence of desire.
It’s the direction of it.
That’s where Jesus draws the line.
And suddenly… the conversation about masturbation can’t stay surface-level anymore.

Because the real question isn’t just “what are you doing?”
It’s “what is your heart chasing while you do it?”
And that’s harder to hide from.
Much harder.
James brings it even closer in James 1:14–15:
“But each person is tempted when he is lured and enticed by his own desire. Then desire when it has conceived gives birth to sin…”
In Greek, “ἐπιθυμία” (epithymia) again appears… desire. Not evil by default… but dangerous when it begins to rule instead of submit.
Even in Hebrew, the word often translated as desire or lust, “תַּאֲוָה” (ta’avah), carries the idea of craving… longing… something that can either align with God’s design or distort it.
That’s the tension.
Desire itself is not sin.
God created the human body.
God created intimacy.
God created longing.
But sin… twists.
It redirects desire inward… isolates it… detaches it from covenant, from love, from self-giving… and turns it into consumption.
That’s where the heart gets involved.
That’s where the Spirit starts knocking.
So does masturbation always involve lust?

Not necessarily in a purely mechanical sense… but in real life, in lived experience… it rarely exists in isolation from the imagination, from fantasy, from internal pursuit of someone not your spouse, from emotional escape, from a craving that seeks satisfaction outside of God’s design.
And that’s the part many don’t want to face.
Because it’s not just about control.
It’s about surrender.
And surrender feels like losing… until you realize what you’re actually being freed from.
Paul writes in 1 Corinthians 6:18:
The Greek word is “πορνεία” (porneia)… not just acts, but a whole category of disordered sexual expression outside God’s covenant intention.
And then he says something even more piercing:
“Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you…?”
Temple.
In Greek: “ναὸς” (naos).
Not a casual dwelling.
A sacred space.
A place where God’s presence lives.
So the question shifts again.
Not “can I get away with this?”
But “what am I doing with what God calls holy?”
And suddenly… this isn’t about shame.
It’s about identity.
You weren’t created to manage sin quietly.
You were created to be transformed completely.
And yes… there are people reading this who feel exposed right now.
Not condemned… exposed.
There’s a difference.
Condemnation pushes you away from God.
Conviction pulls you toward Him.
So if something in you is stirring… that’s not rejection.
That’s invitation.
An invitation to bring what’s hidden into the light.
Because grace doesn’t operate in darkness.
It transforms what is surrendered.
Listen carefully…
Jesus never looked at someone trapped in sin and said, “Hide better.”
He said, “Follow Me.”
That’s the difference between religion and relationship.
And maybe this is where it becomes personal for you.
Not theoretical.
Not theological.
But real.
What are you turning to when you feel alone?
What are you feeding when your mind starts wandering?
What are you allowing your heart to pursue in secret?
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected.
Your honesty might be the beginning of someone else’s freedom too.
Don’t keep this to yourself.
And if you feel something shifting in you right now… don’t walk away from it.
Stay close.
Not as pressure.
As partnership.
Because when you support what spreads the Gospel… you participate in it.
If you’re ready to go deeper… not just informed but transformed…
Because the real question was never just about masturbation.
It was about what your heart is surrendering to… and who you’re becoming in the process.
And Jesus is still rewriting stories… even the ones you’re ashamed to talk about.
Nothing hidden stays hidden when grace steps in.
